html:
Garifuna Settlement Day, 19 November, marks the arrival by canoe of a large group of Garifuna at Stann Creek, now Dangriga, in southern Belize in 1832.

The Garifuna descend from Africans and Island Caribs of St Vincent. Britain deported them in 1797 to Roatán off Honduras, and from there they spread along the coast of Central America. Many fled to the Belize coast after taking the losing side in civil wars in Honduras.

Dangriga became the centre of Garifuna life in Belize, with its own language, punta music and drumming. In 2001 UNESCO listed the language, dance and music of the Garifuna as a masterpiece of oral heritage. The day has been a public holiday since the 1940s, a counterpart to the British story of St. George's Caye.
